# Word Choice

Guidelines for clear, simple, user-friendly language.

## Core Principle

Use simple, precise, conversational words.

## Common Replacements

| Avoid | Use |
|-------|-----|
| utilize | use |
| initiate | start |
| terminate | end, stop |
| facilitate | help |
| leverage | use |
| functionality | feature |
| in order to | to |
| at this point in time | now |
| due to the fact that | because |
| prior to | before |
| subsequent to | after |
| in the event that | if |
| for the purpose of | to |
| with regard to | about |
| in conjunction with | with |

## Contractions

Use common contractions for conversational tone:

- ✅ don't, it's, you'll, we're, can't, won't, isn't, aren't
- ❌ would've, should've (can be misread)
- ❌ ain't, gonna, wanna (too informal)

## Avoid

- **Jargon** — Replace with familiar words
- **Anthropomorphism** — Don't give human traits to systems ("the system thinks")
- **Vague words** — Replace "some," "various," "stuff" with specifics
- **"Please"** — Use only when asking something inconvenient
- **Neologisms** — Avoid newly invented words

## Positive Framing

- ✅ "Keep this box checked"
- ❌ "Don't uncheck this box"
- ✅ "Save your work before closing"
- ❌ "Don't close without saving"

## Action Verbs for UI

| Action | Verb |
|--------|------|
| Mouse/touch interaction | Select (not click, tap, or click on) |
| Keyboard input | Enter, type |
| Toggle on | Turn on |
| Toggle off | Turn off |
| Open menu | Open |
| Close dialog | Close |
| Navigate | Go to |
